The best teacher I ever had was my high school chemistry teacher, Mr. Delgado. He wasn't the funniest or the most popular, but he had a rare talent: he made you feel that your questions were interesting.

When someone asked a question he didn't know the answer to, he would say, "Good. Let's find out." Then we would spend the next ten minutes working it out together. I learned more from those detours then from any textbook.

Years later, I realized he was teaching us something more important then chemistry. He was teaching us that not knowing is the begining of learning, not something to be ashamed of.
